correctness.rationale: For every a,m,t the minimal winning family has precisely m equal-size sets; computing its normalized Deegan–Packel weights yields C(t)=(mt+a)/(m(a+t)^2). The exact subtraction factors as (t-1)[m(a²-t)-a(2a+t+1)] divided by a positive denominator, establishing the iff condition. The sharp supremum t follows from strict two-factor bounding and m=a², a→∞; 13-seat minimality is proved by integer case splits m≤2, a≤3 and the residual bound. A monotone sign polynomial gives one-turn behavior. Fresh exact Fraction verification independently enumerated 880 coalition families; no finite checks are mistaken for infinite proof.

value.rationale: Selective veto subdivision is a natural institutional design action not represented by uniform global replication. Exact classification shows when this action paradoxically concentrates total Deegan–Packel power, gives the sharp t-fold amplification envelope, identifies the minimum original electorate inside a motivated explicit family, and resolves all larger veto-block sizes via one-turn dependence. These are substantive structural implications of the concentration measure and furnish interpretable benchmark voting systems.
